It increments the term, votes for itself, and requests votes.
Peers grant at most one vote after checking the candidate log is current.
The candidate becomes leader only after winning a quorum.

lesson.scenario: Three scheduler nodes elect one job dispatcher for epoch 12.

steps.title: No heartbeat
steps.narration: The prior epoch 11 leader stops sending heartbeats.
steps.outcome: Followers wait for independent randomized deadlines.
steps.invariant: Election timeouts should be randomized to reduce repeated split votes.

steps.title: A becomes candidate
steps.narration: A times out first, advances to epoch 12, and self-votes.
steps.outcome: A begins the election in a newer epoch.
steps.invariant: Messages from epochs below 12 can no longer establish authority.

steps.title: Fresh voter grants
steps.narration: B verifies A is at least as up to date and grants its epoch-12 vote.
steps.outcome: A has a majority of the three voters.
steps.invariant: A voter may grant only one vote in an epoch.

steps.title: Authority published
steps.narration: A assumes leadership and publishes epoch 12.
steps.outcome: Schedulers agree on A as the current leader.
steps.invariant: Leadership is scoped to an epoch, not merely a node identity.

steps.title: Heartbeats stabilize
steps.narration: A sends epoch-12 heartbeats and all timers reset.
steps.outcome: A remains leader while it can reach followers.
steps.invariant: A quorum and fencing are required to prevent an isolated old leader from acting.

production.scenario: A SaaS billing system elects one scheduler pod to scan due invoices each midnight so duplicate charge jobs are not enqueued when Kubernetes restarts pods during the run.
components: Starts the daily invoice scan for all active tenants
Several identical pods are ready to run the billing scan
Tracks the current scheduler epoch and winner
Authoritative list of invoices that should be charged tonight
Carries one charge task per invoice after the winner scans the table
Call the PSP and settle invoices from the queue
Shows which pod is leader and whether failover happened mid-run
flows: The midnight trigger wakes the scheduler deployment and all pods begin contending to run the batch.
Each pod asks the election backend to become the billing leader for the current run.
grant leader epoch 441 to one pod
Only one pod receives the winning epoch, so every follower stays idle instead of scanning invoices too.
The elected pod reads the authoritative invoice table and decides which tenants need charging tonight.
Every due invoice is turned into one queue item from the single active scheduler.
The worker fleet charges cards from the queue without caring which scheduler pod originally won leadership.
If the winning pod dies halfway through the run, operations can see the epoch swap before the replacement pod resumes scanning.
